title: Tesla Rallies 5% Amid SpaceX Merger Speculation; Rivian and SpaceX Rise 3%: Is Tesla's 439x P/E a Warning Sign?
html:
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Merger speculation is lifting Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA | TSLA Price Prediction) stock after the Thanksgiving break, putting a spotlight on how much the market already pays for the company’s earnings. TSLA stock is at $397.87 in midday trading, up 5%. After that gain, the stock is still down 12% year to date (YTD).

The rocket and satellite company on the other side of the reported deal is climbing too. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) stock is at $131.20, up 3%. Electric vehicle (EV) maker Rivian Automotive (NASDAQ:RIVN) is moving higher as well. Rivian stock is trading at $12.07, up 3%.

No deal has been announced, and retail forums are split between traders hoping for a buyout premium and those fearing dilution or terms that favor SpaceX. Both camps are focused on one number for Tesla: the exchange ratio.

What’s Been Reported on Tesla and SpaceX Deal Talks

Tesla and SpaceX have reportedly assembled deal teams. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are advising SpaceX directors Roelof Botha and Randy Glein, while Evercore is advising Tesla Chair Robyn Denholm and directors Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung, the Financial Times reported. The core question is how many SpaceX shares Tesla shareholders would get for each share they own.

HSBC estimates a deal could carry a 33%[1] premium to Tesla’s 30-day average share price, meaning $507 per share. Gary Black of The Future Fund sees a 25%[1] premium, or $481, and warned an all-stock bid could push SpaceX shares below $100. Cathie Wood expects Tesla shareholders to demand a premium, and JPMorgan said a deal could speed SpaceX’s entry into the S&P 500.

The dilution worry traces to SpaceX’s November 25 pledge to contribute one newly issued Class A share to every active Trump Account, a gift Tesla CEO Elon Musk will personally match. Alexandra Merz, a Tesla influencer, noted that the pledge could matter in the negotiations and argued Tesla’s special committee should push for “the best exchange ratio the facts can support.” SpaceX shares rose amid a broader tech rally after Musk stated on November 26 that he’d donate another share to every child in America each year.

Tesla’s 439x Earnings Multiple Raises the Stakes

Tesla trades at a trailing 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 439x. In plain terms, buyers are paying a very large multiple of past profits, so much of the price rests on future growth and deal hopes.

Q3 2026 results from Tesla, reported October 21[2], showed adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.48, exceeding the $0.4511 consensus. Sales at the automaker dropped off 0.2%[2] year over year (YoY) to $28.05 billion. The company’s operating income fell 55.8%[2] YoY to $718 million as research and development spending rose to $2.76 billion from $1.63 billion.

The bulls point to Tesla’s businesses beyond car sales. Subscriptions to Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) software reached 1.74 million[2] from 1.04 million, and Cybercab joined the unsupervised Robotaxi fleet in Austin on September 3. The bears note that battery availability limited deliveries to 486,532[2] vehicles while spending keeps climbing.

How Rivian, Lucid and SpaceX Compare With Tesla

Rivian is rising alongside Tesla while standing outside the merger talks, though the stock remains down 39% YTD. The EV maker builds its R1 and R2 and makes services revenue from a Volkswagen joint venture, but it still runs at a loss.

Another EV maker, Lucid Group (NASDAQ:LCID), is slipping. Lucid is executing a turnaround backed by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, with a lower-priced Midsize platform targeted for the second half of 2027.

SpaceX sits on the other side of the potential deal with a very different mix of launch services, Starlink connectivity and an artificial intelligence (AI) business built around Grok and Cursor. Tesla still makes most of its revenue from vehicles, with energy storage, charging and software in supporting roles.

Tesla Rally Hinges on Merger Terms

Tesla’s next test is whether the talks produce an exchange ratio that rewards its shareholders or tilts toward SpaceX. Terms near HSBC’s or Gary Black’s premium estimates could lift the stock, while stalled talks or SpaceX-friendly terms could leave it leaning on a steep earnings multiple. The company’s next earnings report will test whether robotaxi, software and energy growth can support that valuation.

The bulls see a combined Tesla with more ways to fund robotaxis, robots and AI compute. On the downside, a rally resting on unconfirmed reports could fade quickly if either board walks away. Investors may want to stay cautious until the Tesla-SpaceX exchange ratio resolves.

summary: Tesla shares jump on unconfirmed word of a SpaceX deal, yet one number is worrying both bulls and skeptics. Whether shareholders cash in or get shortchanged depends on terms that nobody has seen.
